_note: How SpeedKills' soldier holds a long gun as other players see it (Phase 27, 27.8; src/game/rifle.ts). The free clips the figures play are a pistol library, and the gun used to hang off the chest with the arms swung at it (figure.json hold, measured on the legacy mannequin): the owner saw the USSO held low, its stock out in front of the shoulder, the left hand open under the barrel. The soldier now stands as a rifleman does: the chest turned so the left shoulder leads, the butt in the right shoulder's pocket, the gun along the look, each hand placed on its hold palm first and turned to it, the fingers closed round it. Lengths in metres, angles in degrees. Measured values are off the bought soldier at its game scale (tools/checks/soldier-hold.ts measures them and fails when these part from the model).
_measured: Off the model in its rest pose, at soldier.json's scale: the upper arm (shoulder to elbow joint) 0.260 m, the forearm (elbow to wrist) 0.268 m, the hand from the wrist to the middle finger's knuckle 0.123 m, the middle finger 0.097 m, the knuckles 0.094 m across from the index finger's to the little finger's; the shoulders 0.490 m apart; the front of the body 0.092 to 0.121 m in front of the right shoulder joint, from level with it to 8 cm under it.
_scale: How much bigger than its own model the soldier's gun is drawn, 1 for most (a gun's own over it in guns). The soldier is a big man in armour: its gloved hand is 0.123 m from the wrist to the middle finger's knuckle and 0.094 m across the knuckles (measured, tools/checks/soldier-hold.ts), about 1.25 times a man's, and the bought guns are modelled at a man's size. A gun with an open grip takes the glove as it is (BOOG); one whose trigger guard closes round the fingers can be too small for it (the USSO's opening is 0.075 m tall, and the glove's four fingers need more), and is drawn the least bigger that its hand fits (tools/figure-fit.ts). Only the figure's gun: the one in your own hands is the first-person arms'.
_support: Where the left hand takes a gun, gun-local metres, when not where the model's own measures put it (a gun's own, in guns; none for most). BOOG's own is the front of its fore-end, 0.84 m in front of the butt. BOOG was held by its box magazine while the arm alone fell short of the fore-end (Milestone 342); the owner, 2026-09-30: "the boogs 3rd person still has the hand grabbing the magazine instead of the hand stop/rail". So BOOG's left hand is on the rail under its fore-end, which runs from 22 to 37 cm in front of the grip, 3 cm wide, its bottom 12 cm under the bore (tools/gun-shape.ts across), at its rear end, 22.5 cm in front of the grip: at the rail's middle (30 cm) the arm fell short at rest and the hold slid back 19%, and aimed on the move 54%, onto the magazine and 15 mm into it. There, with BOOG's shoulder let reach 70 degrees (guns.sentinel.reach; the shared 34 slid it 44% aimed at a sprint, 55 still 17), it does not slide at rest, aimed, looking 35 up or down, running or sprinting aimed, or through a melee (measured on the figure, supportSlide). The shoulder only comes forward as far as a pose needs. ANAKIN's (alternator_smg) is under its receiver ahead of the trigger guard: the receiver's flat underside, 6 cm wide, is 7.5 to 8.5 cm under the bore from 16 to 35 cm in front of the trigger, the guard's front sloping down from 14.5 cm in front, its charging handle (Slide) on the left side 18 to 20 cm in front, 3 to 6 cm under (tools/gun-shape.ts side, the parts' boxes): the palm's middle 20.5 cm in front of the trigger (69 cm from the butt), 1.5 cm under the underside. ANAKIN's shoulder reaches 70 degrees as BOOG's does: measured aimed at a sprint, its hold slid 30% back at the shared 34, 16% at 45, 4% at 55, none at 70 (supportSlide). PANDA's (vinson) is under its handguard, a box 8 to 10 cm wide whose underside is 15 to 16 cm under the bore from 16 to 46 cm in front of the gun's middle (its trigger 4 to 6.7 behind it), the magazine (Clip) inside its back half: the palm's middle 37 cm in front, 83 cm from the butt (the survey's), 1.5 cm under the underside. PANDA's shoulder reaches 85 degrees: measured aimed at a sprint its hold slid 43% back at the shared 34, 25% at 55, 14% at 70 and 3% at 85 (supportSlide), its hold 83 cm from the butt the furthest of the three. BIGANTLER's (mastiff) is under its pump (Pump, 14 to 33 cm ahead of the gun's middle, its underside 13.3 cm under the bore, 3.8 to 4.6 cm wide): the palm's middle under the pump's middle, 24 cm ahead, 1.5 cm under it. BIGANTLER's shoulder reaches 45 degrees: aimed at a sprint its hold slid 14% back at the shared 34, none at 45. REZ's (shotgun) is under its fore-end ahead of its magazine: the fore-end is one block 5 to 6 cm wide from 10 to 42 cm ahead of the gun's middle, its underside 16 cm under the bore, with the long magazine (Clip, 5 to 30.5 cm ahead) flush in its back half; the palm's middle 36 cm ahead, 1.5 cm under the underside, so the hand is on the fore-end and not on the magazine (the owner did not want BOOG's on its magazine). REZ's shoulder reaches 85 degrees: its hold slid 24 to 29% back running and sprinting at the shared 34, 6 to 11% at 55, and with its body solved still 8% aimed at a sprint at 70. CHOOCH's (lstar) is under its barrel shroud, 6 to 9 cm wide from 21 to 41 cm ahead of the gun's middle, its underside 14 cm under the bore, the drum (22 cm across) from 20 cm ahead back: the palm's middle 37 cm ahead, 1.5 cm under the shroud. At 30 cm the left forearm ran past the drum's front edge (57 mm into it at rest, 113 sprinting, measured exactly); from 35 cm out it clears it. CHOOCH's shoulder reaches 70 degrees, its hold 37 cm out.
_blade: The chest's turn to its right, so the left shoulder leads and the support hand reaches the handguard (square on, the left hand is 0.67 m from the USSO's handguard and the arm reaches 0.59): split between spine_02 and spine_03, the neck and head turned back by it so the figure still looks where it aims.
_pocket: Where the butt sits, from the right shoulder joint in the chest's frame at rest: `in` toward the middle of the chest, `down` under the joint, `ahead` in front of it, which is the body's front there (measured, 0.092) and the armour's thickness past it. `adsUp` lifts the butt this much into the shoulder as the figure aims in, and the head leans onto the stock by `adsHead` (down, toward the gun).
_hands: Where each palm goes on the gun and how the hand is turned there, in the gun's own frame (+x its right side, +y up, -z forward). `at` is the palm's middle from the hold point the gun names (its grip, its support); `fwd` the way the hand runs from the wrist to the knuckles; `palm` the way the palm faces. The right hand on the pistol grip: the palm on the grip's right side, the knuckles back from its front so the first phalanges lie along its side and the middle ones cross its front (a glove this size on a thin grip; with the knuckles at the front every curled finger went through it). The left under the fore-end, or BOOG's magazine (support): the palm under it, the hand running across it to the gun's right, the fingers laid up its right side and the thumb up its left.
_reach: How far each shoulder may be brought forward, degrees of the clavicle's swing about its own joint, when the arm alone falls short of its hand's place: a person reaching pushes the shoulder forward. The clavicle is 0.205 m (measured), so 34 degrees brings the shoulder up to 12 cm nearer, only as far as is needed. Without it the left hand's hold slid back along the gun whenever the arm came up short and took the fitted hand into the gun (12 to 20 mm): standing it was running (BOOG's 5.5 cm) or looking down, at 18 degrees; and aimed on the move, where the running clips lean the chest 20 cm forward, the hold still slid a third of the way to the grip until 34 (bots aim as they run: every one of them showed it). The slide (mannequin.ts supportHold) counts this reach first.
_elbows: Which way each elbow points, in the figure's frame (+x its left, +y up, +z its front): the right out to the side and down, the left down and a little in, as a rifleman's are.
_twist: The share of a hand's roll about the forearm the forearm's twist bone takes, so the wrist's skin does not wring round like a sweet wrapper when the hand turns onto the gun.
_together: How far each finger's first joint is swung from its splay toward the middle finger's line, 0 to 1. The bought rig's fingers fan out as a T-pose's do (the splay measured off it, rifle.ts measureRifleRig), and a hand on a gun has them together: laid along the side of a fore-end, fanned they read as a wave. Not all the way: a hand's fingers keep a little fan.
_fingerSize: How big the soldier's fingers are drawn against its model's, each finger scaled about its root (a finger's first knuckle, the thumb's joint at the wrist): the owner, 2026-09-30, first "all fingers in 3rd person should be cut down by like 50% size", then, seeing them at half their thickness (they could not hold the guns at half their size), "change them back to normal size and just make it like 90% of the size it was before". Only the figure's: the arms in your own view keep the model's.
_fist: A closed hand, each finger's three joints, degrees (as fingers): a swap's cup bends its fingers the first person's `curl` of the way to it (swapCup), and a melee's punch closes them to it (melee).
_fingers: Each finger's joints closed toward the palm, degrees, knuckle outward, as tools/figure-fit.ts closed each phalanx onto the gun until its skin touched: the right hand's round the grip, its index finger on the trigger at the crease of its last joint, through the guard (searched onto the trigger part's face: the owner, 2026-09-30, "trigger finger should be on the trigger, not in the ready position", then "more through the hold ... right now its like the very finger tip is the only thing that can press the trigger"), the thumb round the far side; the left's laid up the side of what it holds. A fourth number is the first joint's sideways swing, degrees, about the palm's normal: a finger's before its curl, the thumb's after it (the curled thumb turned round the far side of its hold; rifle.ts).
_lowered: The gun lowered across the body for a sprint or a swap (SpeedKills always sprints, so this is how an enemy is mostly seen): turned down, toward the figure's left and rolled about its own length, about the butt, held `out` (the figure's frame: +x its left, +z its front) from the body so its receiver clears the belly, the left hand taking it its own way (`l`, as in hands), blended in as it drops. `arc` (metres, the figure's frame) is how far out the gun swings at the middle of its way down or up, 4 lo (1 - lo) of it: blended straight between the two carries, BOOG's stock swept through the right upper arm each time a sprint stopped (found by tools/figure-solve.ts rise). A jump out of a sprint keeps this carry (mannequin.ts), so the lowered stage measures one in the air too. Measured through the stride (tools/figure-solve.ts lowered: four moments of a sprint's and two of a run's): fitted at one, BOOG's stock was clean there and 17 mm into the chest a few tenths of a second later. Its left hand stays where it holds the gun; a search that could move it slid it 6 cm along and the palm off it.
_swap: The lowered carry for a swap, which the figure does standing, over the sprint's (`lowered`): turned down, left and rolled, degrees, and held out, metres, as there. One carry for both had the searches trade a runner's arms against a stander's: sprinting clean, swapping the USSO's magazine 39 mm into the belly. The same numbers as the sprint's here; a gun's own in guns, found by tools/figure-solve.ts swap. The USSO's own is turned 32 degrees down: at 26 its magazine went 40 mm into the belly. The swap's phase (mannequin.ts gunSweep) is the first person's own, gunfeel.json guns.<id>.swap: the gun going away phases out over its holster, the new one in over its draw.
_vent: An overheated gun venting (CHOOCH's lockout; the owner, 2026-10-01: other players see it; act code 20): a carry of its own, as `swap` and `air` are, eased in while the vent lasts and out after it, the hands kept on the gun: the muzzle up (`down` negative, degrees), across the body (`left`), canted (`roll`), held off the chest (`out`, metres in the figure's frame). Started from the swap's carry turned muzzle up, then solved (figure-solve.ts vent) and photographed. The guns agent's first-person vent, when it comes, adds its own shares (fparms.json vent) for the soldier to follow.
_swapCup: The swap in place, when the first person's is (fparms.json swap style "cup": rifle.ts SWAP_CUP; the owner, 2026-09-30, the gun phasing out "from the outside going in" and the next "from the inside out", the hands closing round it "like the streetfighter haduken"): the gun stays up in the hands' hold, with no lowered carry, and each hand comes off its hold `move` metres in the gun's frame (+x its right, +y up, +z back), turned toward the gun's middle and its fingers bent toward the `fist` by the first person's own curl, over the first person's own shares of the swap (fparms.json swap.cup). The first person's moves are view metres; these are the figure's, searched over both swaps' moments (each hand's skin in the gun as drawn, the wrists): the right hand 10 cm out, the most before its wrist bends past 60 degrees, and the left 6 cm down, where nearer ones left the cupped fingers in the gun.
_air: The lowered carry in the air, for a jump out of a sprint (which keeps the sprint's carry, mannequin.ts), over the sprint's: the jump's clip tucks the body forward, and carried the sprint's way the USSO was 39 mm into the belly. A gun's own in guns, found by tools/figure-solve.ts air. The swap's and the air's are blended in over the carry's own time, so a swap begun mid-sprint does not snap the gun from one to the other.
_airRate: How fast the air's own carry comes in and goes, per second (an easing rate, as figure.json reach): as fast as the jump's clip tucks the body (its crossfade is 0.18 s). At the carry's own pace (8) the body was tucked round a gun still in the sprint's carry, 39 mm into the belly, as the feet left the ground.
_recoil: A shot's kick on the held gun, at its start (it fades as the figure's kick does, a tenth of a second): the muzzle up, degrees, and the gun driven back beyond the shoulder, metres. None back: the figure's chest already rocks back with a shot (mannequin.ts, the shoulder with it), and driven back 2.5 cm more the butt went 20 mm (the USSO) to 35 mm (BOOG) into the collarbone. Enough to read as a shot at 30 m, not to aim it away.
_throwFor: How long the soldier's grenade throw takes, s, before its hands go back for the gun: the overhand clip's release is at 0.3 s and its arm is through by 0.4. The act itself lasts figure.json throwShown on the wire (0.7), and held to that the arms hung empty for 0.35 s after the release.
_gunBack: How far both hands have come back onto the long gun (the hold's weights, 0 to 1, the slower of the two) when it is shown again after a throw, a heal or a reach for something: until then the hands go to where it will be, the gun hidden. Shown at once, it came back through both hands (23 to 28 mm) while they were still on their way; at 0.85 of the way the right palm was still 3 cm off its grip. At 0.97 it shows about 0.3 s after the hands start back.
_melee: A melee, as the first person's (fparms.json melee: its shares of the swing; the owner, 2026-09-29: "HOLD THE WEAPON WITH THE RIGHT ARM, SWING AT THEM WITH THE LEFT ARM, LEFT ARM SHOULD GO FROM SUPPORTING THE GUN, BACK A BIT TOWARDS THE PLAYERS CHEST, THEN SWING OUT"; rifle.ts PUNCH): the right hand keeps the gun where it is, and the left leaves it round it (`clear`, metres in the figure's frame at the most, a third of the way off and back on: down and a little to the figure's right, since its fingers hook over the gun's far side; bowed out to its left, they dragged 18 to 24 mm through the gun as it left and came back), draws back to `chest` beside the body with its elbow toward `chestElbow` (low and out), punches out to `out` with the elbow toward `outElbow`, its palm turning from `palmChest` (a vertical fist) to `palmOut` (flat, landed) and its knuckles from `fwdChest` to `fwdOut`, and comes back onto the gun, its fingers closing to the `fist` as it goes. Places in the figure's frame (+x its left, +y up, +z its front, metres from its feet), from the soldier as measured: the left shoulder at 0.17, 1.44, 0.07, the arm 0.53 m. Drawn back, the knuckles lie along the forearm's way in from the elbow: pointed straight ahead, the wrist bent 81 degrees, and along it 43 (searched over both guns' swings). It had been a strike with the gun in both hands, which the first person's no longer is. `time` is the game's melee, s (viewmodel.ts MELEE_TIME; tools/checks/soldier-hold.ts holds them equal): a string of punches goes on from one to the next. PANDA's left hand bows 22 cm down (its own melee.punch.clear): its magazine and the block behind it hang 16.5 cm under the bore between its hold and the chest, and at the shared 15 its fingers dragged 22 mm through them leaving and returning (three punches, measured as the skfigure e2e does; 4 at 22, with the left wrist at 48 degrees). BIGANTLER's bows 8 cm out and 22 cm down: at the shared path its fingers landed 20 mm into the pump coming back (2 so, the left wrist at 41 degrees). REZ's bows 8 cm out at the shared depth: at the shared path its fingers caught its fore-end, 10 mm (2 so).
_reload: The reload as other players see it (rifle.ts reloadPlanOf), the first person's own (the owner, 2026-09-30: "the first and third person final forms agree with each others animations and movements when they reload for the boog and the usso"): its timing is read from the guns agent's fparms.json reload at run time, shares of the gun's empty reload time (weapons.ts reloadEmptyTime), so an enemy's plays from the moment their "reload" arrives. Which reload it is goes with it (the owner, 2026-09-30: "a reload differentiator for empty mag vs still 1 in the chamber"): from empty (act code 9, the figure's `reloadEmpty`) the whole of it over the empty time; a tactical one, a round still chambered, over the gun's tactical time, and where fparms.json has `reload.tactical` its own plan, the empty one's beats in seconds (the point, the magazine out and in, the hand `back` to the fore-end, no rack or bolt: rifle.ts tacticalOf). The gun turns its magazine toward the left hand (`tilt`) as the left hand leaves the fore-end and points at the magazine (the `point` key, its fingers `pointFingers`); the magazine slides down its own length and phases out, a new one phases in from there and slides home, and seats with a kick (`seatKick` of a shot's, gone over `seatKickFor` s), all in the gun: the soldier used to pull it, drop a copy to the floor and fetch a new one from a pouch at the hip, which the first person never did. Then the hands work the gun as its pack gun does: the USSO's left hand racks the charging handle (`handle`, `handleBack`), BOOG's left goes back to the fore-end and its right works the bolt (`bolt`, `boltUp`, `boltBack`) over the shares of the rack in `bolt` (the L96X clip's bolt at 0.30 to 0.48 of its 0.22 to 0.56 window, 0.235 to 0.765 of the rack). A key may have fingers of its own (`fingers`, as the hold's; the point's are `pointFingers`), blended in as the hand goes to it: at the USSO's charging handle the hold's, laid along the fore-end, stood 25 mm off the gun, and searched onto it there (tools/figure-solve.ts KEYFINGERS=1) they lie on it, the palm still 12 to 17 mm into the receiver. `keys` are palm places and turns off the magazine's bottom (`mag`, carried with it as it slides), the charging handle or bolt (`handle`) or the grip, with `fwd` and `palm` as in `hands`.
_aim: Aimed in, the gun comes up so its own sight line (gunmodels.ts sightY and rearF, the eye point the first-person view aims down) runs through the soldier's right eye (measured off its eye meshes, rifle.ts rightEye): the rear sight `relief` in front of the eye and the line `cheek` under its middle, the head leant onto the stock first (pocket.adsHead). At rest the butt is in its pocket; the two are blended by how far the figure aims in. `side` sets the sight line that far to the figure's right of the eye, the head leant over to it (pocket.adsHead toward): lined up on the eye itself, the stock ended in the middle of the chest, where a shooter's never is.
_guns: A gun's own numbers over the ones above, where its shape needs them: its hands by tools/figure-fit.ts (each hand closed round its hold at the place searched round a start measured off the gun, tools/gun-shape.ts), its pocket, turn, elbows and aim by tools/figure-solve.ts rest, against the frame sheets. Measured, gun frame, cm: the USSO's pistol grip, its magazine inside it, hangs from 8 to 18 cm under the bore (the magazine on to 28), 3.4 cm thick and raked back 19 degrees, inside a trigger guard that closes round the fingers (an opening 7.5 cm tall and 4 cm deep, the trigger in its top), and its fore-end is a slab 2.4 to 4.2 cm wide down to 12 cm under the bore; BOOG's grip hangs from 15 to 24 cm under, 4 cm thick and raked back 25 degrees, its trigger in a small loop in front of its top, and its box magazine, 15 cm long and 3 cm wide, hangs to 18.5 cm under in front of the loop. A palm's middle is 1.5 cm inside the hand, so it sits that far off the surface it holds. ANAKIN's pistol grip holds its magazine too (Clip, 9.5 to 29 cm under the bore, raked back about 35 degrees, 3.6 to 4 cm thick where the hand is), its trigger 4.5 cm in front of the grip's top inside a guard whose front slopes from 14.5 cm in front at the bore to 2.5 cm in front 19 cm under, a stock reaching 48 cm behind the trigger. Its right hand holds the grip's top with the magazine running on below it, as an Uzi's: a search from the shared start laid the hand flat on the receiver's side with straight fingers, so it was placed from the USSO's fitted hand carried over by each gun's trigger and grip, and grasped there (figure-fit.ts SEARCH=0). PANDA's grip hangs from 6 to 22 cm under the bore behind its trigger, 4 cm thick at the top and 6 lower down, open behind it until the stock starts 25 cm back (a skeleton stock, 4 cm wide): its right hand was placed from the USSO's fitted hand carried over by the trigger and grasped there, the index 4 mm off the trigger's face; a search from there moved it 3.5 cm back and took the index 30 mm off. Its lower fingers stop on the thick grip's front rather than wrapping it. PANDA's carries: its left hand keeps the hold's own place (lowered.l): a search put it 3.6 cm up into the handguard (22 mm of skin in the gun sprinting) where the hold's own is 5. Its sprint and jump carries were solved counting the left hold's slide (figure-solve.ts): solved without it, the muzzle went 44 degrees down, the arm fell short, and the hold slid back into the magazine. BIGANTLER's grip hangs behind its trigger (the trigger 12 to 14 cm behind the gun's middle), 2 to 3 cm thick and raked back; its right hand placed from the USSO's carried over by the trigger (7 cm behind it, 3.5 under) and grasped there, the index's crease 0.2 mm off the trigger; the left closed round the pump. REZ's grip hangs behind its trigger (the trigger 6.5 to 11 cm behind the gun's middle), raked back; its right hand placed from the USSO's carried over by the trigger, then searched from there (the placed grasp's ring finger hung 12 mm off the grip), the index's crease 0.1 mm off the trigger. CHOOCH's grip is a slanted bar in a thumbhole stock, the drum close in front: its finger space is 5 cm deep and 8 tall, closed below by the guard's bar, too small for the soldier's glove to wrap (drawn 1.15 or 1.25 times as big, no better). Its right palm sits behind the bar, the index's crease on the trigger (0.0 mm); a grasp left the ring and pinky straight out along the frame (3 mm in, a finger gun from the side), so they are curled round the bar instead, 18 mm into the guard's frame where nothing outside shows it (photographed from the right and the front). A pistol joins the rig with `stance` "pistol" (rifle.ts pistolStance): its `pocket` is not the shoulder's but in front of the chest at the arms' reach, its `aim.relief` the arms' length from the eye (APUHTHEE 0.36, measured: at 0.45 the right arm was straight with the palm 7.4 cm short of its place, at 0.40 still 2.5 short; at 0.36 the elbow is at 169 degrees and the hand on it), the chest turned less (`blade`), the head not down onto a stock (`adsHead`), and its own low carry (`lowered`). APUHTHEE's hands (Milestone 472): the right searched on the handle, the index's crease on the trigger; the left round the right, its palm on the right fingers, its fingers over them and its thumb forward along the frame under the slide (the index curled and the thumb laid by hand, each measured against the gun and the right hand, figure-audit.js handOnHand: the fit had left the index straight out and the thumb up the slide's side). STRYDER's pistol (`autopistol`, Milestone 482, fitted ahead of its roster change): aimed at 0.34 m (at 0.36 the palm was 1.2 cm short, the elbow straight), drawn 1.1 times as big (the least at which the glove's index gets into its hook of a guard onto the trigger: at 1.05 its crease stopped 14.7 mm off), the right palm kept 4 mm off the handle where the index reaches the trigger (seated on it, 13 mm short), its pinky under the handle's bottom. The left palms (the owner, 2026-10-05: "the left support hand on the USSO has a gap"): each palm touches its hold, its nearest tenth 7 to 16 mm off (figure-audit.js palmFlush), the glove's palm cupped under a fore-end; BOOG's pressed 9 mm onto its rail (12 to 5 mm), where pressing the USSO's or CHOOCH's only sank it in. The low carries' own left hands, PANDA's 11 mm and ANAKIN's 7 off their guns, are the fitted ones now. HAEFY (`3030`, Milestone 500) wears BOOG's bought model in its own skins (paidweapons.json), so it is held as BOOG is, a copy of BOOG's fitted numbers, held to every skfigure check as its own gun; if HAEFY becomes the launcher (docs/PLAN_THE_EIGHT_GUNS.md 5.7) it is fitted from scratch then.
